etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: The adjective is derived from Late Middle English pievish, peuysche, pevish, pevysh (“capricious, wilful; perverse, wayward”); further etymology uncertain, possibly from one of the following:
The adverb is derived from the adjective.
senses: Constantly complaining, especially in a childish way due to insignificant matters; fretful, whiny.
Quick to become bad-tempered or cross, especially due to insignificant matters; irritable, pettish, petulant. [from 16th c.]
(obsolete) Synonym of peevishly (“in a peevish manner: whiningly; irritably, petulantly; etc.”).
